blocks.title: <ico-recycle></ico-recycle> REPASO EXPRESS · B1 final
blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la última clase de B1. Une cada expresión con su significado, sin mirar atrás.

pairs.l: by the end of the month

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> I'VE DONE vs I'VE BEEN DOING
blocks.intro: En una entrevista cuentas tu experiencia con dos formas: el present perfect simple para resultados que se pueden contar y el continuous para lo que sigues haciendo. Después, el método STAR para contar una historia en cuatro líneas.

vocab.en: Tell me about a time when…
vocab.sp: cuéntame de una vez en que…

vocab.en: What would you say is your biggest strength?
vocab.sp: ¿cuál dirías que es tu mayor fortaleza?

vocab.en: Where do you see yourself in five years?
Do you have any questions for us?

blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , comparar , escucha , ordenar , diálogo y completar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · RESULTADOS QUE SE CUENTAN — have + participio

items.sp: Dirigí tres lanzamientos (y cuentan para hoy).

items.en: I've managed two teams so far.
items.sp: Hasta ahora he dirigido dos equipos.

items.en: We've cut delivery times by half.
items.sp: Redujimos los tiempos de entrega a la mitad: un resultado.

parts.html: 2 · ALGO QUE SIGUES HACIENDO — have been + -ing, con for / since

items.en: I've been leading the daily standups since March.
items.sp: Dirijo las reuniones diarias desde marzo, y sigo.

items.en: I've been working with this client for a year.
items.sp: Trabajo con este cliente desde hace un año.

items.en: How long have you been working here?

parts.body: for + cuánto tiempo (for a year) · since + cuándo empezó (since March). En español dices «trabajo aquí desde 2022», en presente: I work here since 2022. → I've been working here since 2022.

parts.html: 3 · VERBOS DE ESTADO: SIEMPRE SIMPLE — know, want, believe, have (tener)

items.en: I've known Priya for five years.
items.sp: Conozco a Priya desde hace cinco años.

items.en: I've always wanted to lead a team.

parts.body: Un estado no es una actividad: no lleva -ing. I've been knowing her for years. → I've known her for years.

parts.html: 4 · STAR EN CUATRO LÍNEAS — Situation, Task, Action, Result

items.en: Last year, our website crashed on launch night.
items.sp: S · la situación, en pasado simple.

items.en: My task was to get it back online fast.
items.sp: T · tu tarea, en pasado simple.

items.en: I checked the logs and restarted the payment service.
items.sp: A · lo que hiciste tú: pasado simple con «I».

items.en: As a result, the site was back in an hour, and we've had no downtime since.
items.sp: R · el resultado, en pasado + present perfect para lo que sigue siendo cierto.

parts.html: 5 · VERBOS FUERTES PARA LA ACCIÓN — que se note que fuiste tú

items.en: I took ownership of the problem.
I stepped up when my manager was away.
items.sp: Di un paso al frente cuando mi jefa no estaba.

items.en: I oversaw the move to the new server.
items.sp: Supervisé el cambio al nuevo servidor.

parts.html: TRAMPA DEL ESPAÑOL — palabras que parecen iguales y no lo son

items.en: Currently, I'm leading a team of four.
I have a degree in marketing.
items.sp: «Carrera universitaria» = degree. Career es tu trayectoria profesional.

items.en: I attended the training in May.

items.sp: La edad va con be, nunca con have.

parts.body: Actually I work in sales. → Currently, I work in sales. · I have thirty years. → I'm thirty.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE PROMOTION
blocks.intro: Después del gran pitch, Priya abre un puesto nuevo: Team Lead. Marcos se postula… y también Carla, una candidata de afuera con un currículum muy fuerte. Primero, una entrevista de práctica con Priya.

blocks.title: INTERVIEW WORDS · toca para girar
blocks.intro: Las palabras que se escuchan en cualquier entrevista en inglés. Aparecen en los audios.

cards.back: que trabaja bien con fechas límite
habilidades que sirven en otro puesto

cards.front: a strength / an area to improve

blocks.title: I'VE WRITTEN vs I'VE BEEN WRITING
blocks.intro: Las dos hablan del mismo informe, pero una mira el resultado y la otra la actividad. ¿Cómo sabes si está terminado?

items.q: ¿Cuál dice que el informe está terminado?
Estás cansado y tu café se enfrió. ¿Cuál explica por qué?
¿Cuál puede seguir con «…and I've sent it to Priya»?
Priya: «How many reports have you written this week?» ¿Qué respondes?
Son las once y empezaste a las nueve. Todavía no terminaste. ¿Qué dices?
options: I've been writing the report since nine.
I've written the report since nine.
I write the report since nine.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE INTERVIEW
blocks.desc: Entrevista de práctica: Priya le pide a Marcos una historia de algo que salió mal. Él elige la noche en que se cayó el sitio.

questions.q: Which of Marcos's experiences is still going on?
What did Marcos do on the night of the crash?
options: He called the client to explain the problem
He asked Sofia to restart the server
He found the problem in the logs and restarted the payment service

questions.q: What does Priya's last comment imply?
options: He should talk about his own actions
He should give more credit to Sofia

questions.q: What was the result of his action?
options: The site was down all night, but the client didn't notice
The site was back in about an hour, with no downtime since
The client complained, but renewed the contract

speaking.prompt: Retell Marcos's crash story as a STAR answer in four sentences, using 'I' for the Action.
speaking.starter: Last year, (situation). My task was to (task). I (action) and I (action). As a result, (result), and we've had no downtime since.

transcript.html: Thanks for coming in, Marcos. I know it's strange to be interviewed by your own manager, so let's keep it simple. Tell me about a time something went wrong at work.
Sure. Last year, on the night of the GreenMarket launch, the website crashed at about eleven o'clock. Sofia called me, and the site was completely down.
I remember that night. What was your task?

My task was to get the site back online before the client noticed. So we logged on, we checked the logs, and we found the problem: the payment system was sending too many requests. We restarted the payment service, and we stayed online until everything was stable.
The result? The site was back in about an hour, and the client never noticed. We've had no downtime since.
Good. Now, a Team Lead does more than fix problems. What are you doing now that shows you're ready?
Well, I've been leading the daily standups since March. And I've handled three launches, so I know what can go wrong, and when.
That's useful. One more thing. In your crash story, you said "we" a lot. We logged on, we found it, we restarted it. Who is "we"?
Oh. Well, Sofia called me, but I found the problem, and I restarted the service. That part was me.
Then say "I", Marcos. The panel can't promote "we".

blocks.title: BUILD THE ANSWER
blocks.intro: La primera es una respuesta STAR completa: ordena las cuatro partes. Las demás son frases de entrevista.

words: Last year, our website crashed on launch night.
My task was to get it back online fast.
I checked the logs and restarted the payment service.
As a result, we've had no downtime since.
items.answer: Last year, our website crashed on launch night. My task was to get it back online fast. I checked the logs and restarted the payment service. As a result, we've had no downtime since.
I've been working here for two years
How long have you been leading the team?
I took ownership of the problem

blocks.title: YOU'RE THE CANDIDATE
blocks.intro: Priya te entrevista. Una respuesta es demasiado modesta, otra suena arrogante y una es la correcta.

lines.html: So, why do you want this role?

options: I don't know if I'm ready, but I can try.
I've been leading the standups since March, and I'm ready for more.
Honestly, I'm the best person here. It's obvious.

lines.html: What would you say is your biggest strength?

options: I handle pressure well. During the crash, I stayed calm and fixed it in an hour.
Delegating. I've been sharing more tasks with the team since spring.
There are too many to list, honestly.
My setbacks are always someone else's fault.
A launch slipped by a week. I took ownership and told the client early.
I'd rather not talk about failures.

lines.html: Do you have any questions for us?

options: When do I get the bigger salary?
Yes. What would success look like in the first six months?

blocks.title: SIMPLE OR CONTINUOUS?
blocks.intro: Elige la forma correcta: resultado que se cuenta, actividad que sigue, o verbo de estado.

items.q: We've been testing the new app ___ two weeks.
You look tired. — Yes, I ___ on this report since eight.
Marcos ___ the daily standups since March.

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE FEEDBACK
blocks.desc: Esa noche, Sofia le deja un mensaje de voz a Marcos: dos cosas que hizo bien y dos que tiene que arreglar antes del panel.

questions.q: Which two things did Marcos do well?
options: A clear structure and strong numbers

questions.q: How long did the crash story take?
What does Sofia want him to practice tonight?
options: The crash story, with more detail

questions.q: What does Sofia suggest about the panel?
options: It wants to hear about the whole team
It cares about what Marcos did himself

speaking.prompt: Do Sofia's exercise: answer 'Tell me about a time you handled pressure' in 30 seconds, using 'I' every time.
speaking.starter: Last (month / year), (situation). I had to (task), so I (action). As a result, (result).

transcript.html: Hi Marcos, it's Sofia. Priya told me about your practice interview, and it's mostly good news. Two things went really well. Your crash story had a clear structure: situation, task, action, result. And your numbers were strong. Three launches, no downtime since. That's a track record. But there are two things to fix before the panel. First, your answers are too long. Priya timed you, and the crash story took nearly four minutes. Keep every answer under two. Second, stop saying "we". The panel wants to know what you did, not what the team did. So here's your homework for tonight: one answer, thirty seconds, and use "I" every time. Call me if you want to rehearse. Good luck!

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> MY STAR STORY
blocks.intro: Escribe tu respuesta a «Tell me about a time something went wrong at work» (5–7 frases), con el método STAR.
checklist: Situación y tarea en pasado (I was working at… / My task was to…)
Acción con I, no con we, y al menos un verbo fuerte (I took ownership / I oversaw)
Resultado concreto, con un número si puedes
Una frase con I've + participio (resultado) y una con I've been + -ing + for/since
blocks.example: In año, I was working at empresa / puesto when qué pasó. My task was to tu tarea. I acción 1 and acción 2. As a result, resultado. Since then, I've participio + lo que sigue.
blocks.hw: Escribe tu historia y después grábate contándola en menos de dos minutos, sin leer. Envíame texto y audio por WhatsApp.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna y la historia tiene las cuatro partes de STAR.
Usaste I've done y I've been doing bien, con for / since, y la acción está contada con I.
Un lector lo entiende sin releer: ideas unidas con conectores, sin traducir literal del español.
